title: IQM Announces Zero-Downtime Upgrade Program for Halocene Product Line Scaling Past 1,000 Qubits - Quantum Computing Report
author: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
text:
IQM Quantum Computers (Nasdaq: IQMX) has unveiled an on-premises upgrade program for its IQM Halocene quantum error-correction product line at the SC26 supercomputing conference in Chicago, establishing a hardware migration path from its initial 150-qubit processor to future systems exceeding 1,000 qubits. Designed for high-performance computing (HPC) centers and enterprise data centers, the program bundles IQM’s HPC integration service with each hardware transition so facilities can scale physical qubit capacity without interrupting active workloads.

Under the deployment model, IQM installs and commissions each next-generation Halocene unit alongside an existing system before decommissioning the older hardware, maintaining continuity across software toolchains, Slurm-based HPC job schedulers, and GPU interconnects. Built on an open, modular error-correction stack integrated with NVIDIA CUDA-Q Logical that leverages real-time QEC decoding over NVIDIA NVQLink, the architecture allows customers to pair local quantum processors with existing CPU and GPU clusters for hybrid AI and simulation workflows while preserving data residency on site.

First introduced in November 2025, IQM’s Halocene logical-qubit roadmap was selected by the LUMI AI Factory, coordinated by CSC – IT Center for Science, to deploy the LUMI-IQ superconducting system for hybrid HPC and AI acceleration alongside the upcoming LUMI-AI supercomputer. The program builds on IQM’s 10 supercomputing integrations completed since 2021, including multi-generation upgrades at Finland’s VTT (from 5 to 53 qubits) and four systems at Germany’s Leibniz Supercomputing Centre (LRZ), including Europe’s Euro-Q-Exa system. While IQM has not yet disclosed target delivery dates or logical-qubit specifications for the 1,000-qubit milestone, the program provides a defined procurement path for centers adopting early error-correction hardware.
